lesson.title: Choosing Loop Structures
lesson.driving_question: How can the reason for repetition determine which loop structure to use?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Choosing and combining count-controlled and condition-controlled loops
lesson.concept_budget: Compare and combine already-taught for and while structures without introducing another loop form.
misconceptions: A for loop suits a known repetition count.
A while loop suits repetition controlled by a condition.
A while-loop control value must change.
The loop body is the indented block.
lesson.progression_note: Integrates the two Grade 6 loop families before the recap-style capstone.
code_expectations: selection may appear inside a loop

primm.prompt: Recall when range() fixes the number of repeats and why a while-loop control value must change.
Use answers wait and done. Predict the warm-up numbers, the number of prompts, and the final message.
Run with wait then done. Mark which output came from the counted loop and which interaction came from the condition loop.

questions: Which loop runs exactly three times, and which part of the code sets that limit?
What happens if answer = input(...) is moved outside the while loop?
Why does range(1, 4) display 1, 2 and 3 rather than four values?
If the user enters DONE instead of done, why does the condition-controlled loop repeat?

primm.prompt: Change the example so it first asks how many warm-up rounds to show and stores the whole number in [rounds]. Use [rounds] in range() so the for loop shows that many rounds. The while loop should still end when the user types "done".

Create [counter] and store 0 in it before the while loop. Add 1 to [counter] each time the user enters an answer, including "done". After "done" is entered, display "Answers entered:" followed by [counter]. Test "wait", "wait", then "done"; display "Answers entered: 3".

Create a training program. Use a for loop to display "Exercise 1" to "Exercise 4". Then use a while loop to ask for whole-number effort scores until the user enters 0. Count every score except 0 and display "Scores entered:" with the count.
Repair the range end and update answer inside the while loop so the program displays three rounds and can terminate.

blocks.definition: A fixed number of repetitions known before the loop begins.
A test that decides whether a while loop repeats.
A change to a value used by the loop condition.
Selecting a loop structure that matches why repetition ends.
A special input that signals the end of repeated input.

programs.challenge1:
rounds = int(input("How many warm-up rounds? "))
for round_number in range(1, rounds + 1):
    print("Warm-up round", round_number)
answer = ""
while answer != "done":
    answer = input("Type done to finish: ")
print("Session complete.")
programs.challenge2:
for round_number in range(1, 4):
    print("Warm-up round", round_number)
answer = ""
counter = 0
while answer != "done":
    answer = input("Type done to finish: ")
    counter = counter + 1
print("Answers entered:", counter)
